summary: June nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000 — roughly half of expectations — lifting stocks as traders dialed back Fed rate-hike bets. Market expectations for a July FOMC rate hike have since pulled back to 20% from 30% last week. Meanwhile, the Trump administration chose not to extend the USMCA trade deal, leaving North American trade terms in limbo and sustaining a cloud over risk assets even as equities grind higher.
tweet: Weak jobs print (57K vs. ~115K est.) has cooled July rate-hike odds to 20%, while USMCA expiry adds a fresh trade uncertainty overhang across assets.
